findings.description: 'SHOULD' is used for a PolicyGuard rejection rule that governs fail-closed behavior. Normative safety requirements must use 'MUST' to be unambiguous and enforceable.

evidence.quote: PolicyGuard SHOULD reject when data is missing.

findings.proposed_fix: Replace 'SHOULD' with 'MUST': 'PolicyGuard MUST reject when data is missing.'

findings.description: AT-999 is cited as a bare inline reference with no corresponding acceptance test definition, anchor, or CONTRACT.md entry verifiable from this fixture. Broken AT references undermine contract traceability.
findings.proposed_fix: Define AT-999 with a proper anchor in CONTRACT.md and link the clause to it, or remove the reference if no such AT exists.

findings.description: The rejection clause does not specify which trading mode (ReduceOnly or Kill) the system must enter when data is missing, leaving the fail-closed terminal state undefined.

evidence.quote: PolicyGuard SHOULD reject when data is missing.

findings.proposed_fix: Extend the clause to specify the resulting mode, e.g. 'PolicyGuard MUST reject and set TradingMode=ReduceOnly when required data is absent or stale.'
